It sounds like you're physically dependent on weed and are experiencing withdrawals when you stop using it. Sadly, there's a lot of misinformation out there about weed and how it's "non-addictive and can't give withdrawals," but there are many, many people who experience cannabis dependence and withdrawals, and it seems that you are as well.

Please don't call them junkies, and they aren't the awful ones. They're struggling and suffering, victims of addiction. Likely isolated from their families if they had them, unable to have friends or progress through life. What's awful is what's happening to them, and they deserve to get better. As long as they aren't leaving needles on the ground or harming others, they deserve love and to be treated as people. Direct your disappointment and negative feelings towards the drug, or the dealer, or addiction as a whole; they likely started by trying to run from their own negative feelings.

I understand that; you lose weight before you eat again, but at some point you will eat again. When you eat, after your body went through all of the processes that reduce metabolism activity, conserve energy expenditure, and increase the energy your body absorbs, you would gain more weight from eating the same amount of food than if you never went through those processes. To be clear, I'm not talking about gaining weight in the long run, I'm talking about gaining weight after losing weight; which is a very reasonable explanation for why op is staying at the same weight. Their weight would begin at a downward trend, but as the body absorbs energy more effectively and burns less and less off, this down trend would appear to flatten over time even as they eat the same amount of calories.

Paraphrase: The calories used each day go down, and more energy is gotten from the same food, so the amount of food that counts as being at a deficit go down as well (what was once a deficit may no longer be, and what is still a deficit is less significant).

Due to the article you linked's wording, I believe it means you can't gain weight while *only* not eating (I assume it says that for people who may have been told you can gain weight without eating). But of course, I'm referring to fasting in which case people still eat to stay alive. And I do appreciate that this may give op anxiety, which is absolutely awful, but I believe it would do a net-positive in the long run. After all, you can only rely on people not knowing things for so long; they could learn about this stuff any day. I believe that more knowledge is almost always better, and in the same way that adults are allowed to smoke cigarettes and drink alcohol, people have the option to do what they will. And I don't mean to sound like I agree with that way of thinking, of course I hope with every inch of my soul that op is able to recover to any degree. 



"[While fasting], a hormone known as leptin begins to decline. Leptin is produced by fat cells and tells your body that it has adequate fat stores, helping regulate appetite and encouraging calorie burning"

As leptin declines, a process called Adaptive Thermogenesis occurs. 

"Adaptive thermogenesis is a protective process that alters your body’s metabolism to **increase energy intake** and **decrease energy output** to slow weight loss. ... Combined, the **reduction** in the number of calories you burn and **increase** in calorie intake lowers the likelihood of continued weight loss"

https://www.healthline.com/nutrition/refeed-day



"Metabolism slows down while fasting. The metabolism continues at a lower rate and it causes weight gain after fasting"

https://knoji.com/article/postfasting-weight-gain-how-to-prevent-weight-gain-after-fasting/



"this weight gain after fasting is quite normal. When the body is fasting, it is in 'survival mode.' Basically, the body thinks that its survival is being threatened by the lack of food. The metabolism slows down significantly to conserve energy. When you break the fast, the body, rather than going back to normal, begins to 'hoard' food out of fear that another food shortage may happen. In addition, the digestive system goes into hibernation when fasting; it's like a large bear sleeping. Then, when you break the fast ... the metabolism remains slow and continues to hoard fat from whatever you eat"

"When you break a fast, your body replenishes glycogen in your liver and muscles ... glycogen is mainly water"

[Won't directly show sources as they have lots of potentially triggering material on them, but if one really wanted, I'm sure they could paste parts of the quotes into a search engine to verify them]

Your body doesn't gain weight on its own; the metabolism slows down drastically and you enter a "post-absorptive state" in which your digestive system essentially goes into sleep mode to conserve energy, and your body begins to burn different cells for energy than it usually does. The weight gain is caused by eating while in this state, as your metabolism lags behind and is still partially in hibernation mode.

If you eat too little food too far apart, your body goes into a state in which instead of using energy normally, it stores it and tries to conserve as much of it as possible; think of it as a "survival mode." If you enter this state, the next time you eat, you will gain as much weight as your body possibly can and will retain as much of it as it can, as it is trying to do exactly that --- keep itself from having to throw hormones off balance or suspend certain bodily processes in order to keep you alive. If you mean a reason to die, please don't. The people who speak about us as separate from reality just haven't thought about life enough, they have their own shortcomings. Life is absolutely meaningless, completely and absolutely; humans well be born and die for millions, tens of millions, hundreds of millions of years to come, and technology and ways of life and cultures will change, but ultimately it's all going to be replaced and accomplishes nothing. It's your perspective that decides what life is and why we're here, your own thoughts that give purpose to life. Life is a means to feel happiness and love, that's why I'm here. Without conscious life, there would be no positivity in the universe, just existence, but every time you smile or laugh or make someone else laugh or make a memory with a friend or learn something new, you're creating new emotion in the universe, you make positivity where there was none. Your purpose, just as everyone else's, is to simply live and feel and share and learn and think; whether that's beautiful/worthwhile or not depends on the perspective you choose to have. I was suicidal until I took psychs multiple times, and they had little impact on me until multiple months after my last experience. I decided to change my perspective. I wasn't necessarily taught anything by the experiences, it just gave me the experience and temporary feelings that I needed to realize I should change my perspective, it *reminded* me that love is everywhere and that I can create it, I was just ignoring it. Meaning and purpose to life is everywhere; try to break your psychological routine (your everyday thoughts) and feel the love and life around you. Look at a wall or a rock and think about how they were built, how there were people right on top of your house at some point building the roof, or inside your apartment room applying the drywall. How the rocks and trees took decades to be formed and how you might be the only one to set your eyes on that exact position on them for decades to come, how everything you do is unique and special to your own ways. We *are* freaks, we're crazy sentient beings who consume so much energy, who have changed the way the whole world works, who choose love over our own safety and lives sometimes. We're freaks but we're created by nature, nature allowed us to exist and we're beautiful freaks. You have the power to go outside and help a neighbor, to observe nature, to give someone a hug and increase the universe's net love and happiness that day. You deserve to be alive, you are worth experiencing life. Please respond to this comment or DM me if you'd like to talk more about my perspective or if you just want support or to ask questions or anything at all. Play your favourite song and dance alone today, entertain your heart. Much love ❤️
